title: Non-Canonical Quantum Otto Engine
abstract: The fast-developing quantum technology is propelling thermal machine, which lies at the heart of thermodynamics, into a new golden era. Being stochastic because of the non-negligible thermal and quantum fluctuations, the efficiency and power of a finite-time quantum heat engine exhibit a trade-off, preventing the simultaneous achievement of high power and high efficiency. Conventional studies treat the statistics of a heat engine by assuming canonical thermalization, which is valid only under weak-coupling conditions. We here investigate the noncanonical effect on the statistics of the efficiency and power for a finite-time quantum Otto cycle. It is revealed that their average values and variances are highly controllable by engineering the energy spectrum structure of the composite system consisting of the working substance and the bath. Near the quantum critical point induced by the formation of a bound state in the energy spectrum, the average efficiency and power can be boosted simultaneously, meanwhile, both of their variances are decreased. Deepening our understanding of the usefulness of quantum reservoir engineering in thermodynamics, our result lays the foundation for the realization of efficient and stable quantum energy devices.
summary: This paper analyzes a quantum Otto engine, focusing on how non-Markovian thermalization affects its performance statistics. By moving beyond the standard Born-Markov approximation, the authors show that engineering the system's energy spectrum near a quantum critical point allows for the simultaneous enhancement of efficiency and power while reducing fluctuations. This suggests a new pathway for designing stable and highly efficient quantum energy devices.
main_problem: The study investigates the non-canonical effects on the statistical properties (average values and variances) of efficiency and power in a finite-time quantum Otto cycle, moving beyond the limitations of standard canonical thermalization assumptions.
main_result: The average efficiency and power can be simultaneously boosted while decreasing their variances by engineering the energy spectrum structure, particularly near a quantum critical point induced by a bound state formation.
method: The authors use characteristic functions and detailed derivations of expectation values ($\langle W angle, \langle Q angle, \langle W^2 angle$) to compare exact non-Markovian results against the standard Born-Markov approximations.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum Otto engine where the working substance is treated as a quantum harmonic oscillator coupled to hot and cold thermal baths. The dynamics are governed by master equations and quantum Langevin equations.
key_observables: Average efficiency ($\langle \eta angle$), average power ($\langle P angle$), and their respective variances ($\epsilon^2_\eta, \epsilon^2_P$).
important_parameters: The energy spectrum structure, the proximity to a quantum critical point, and the coupling strength (non-Markovian vs. Born-Markov regime).
main_assumptions: The analysis explicitly contrasts the non-Markovian regime with the Born-Markov approximation, which is assumed to break down under strong coupling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the quantum Otto cycle diagram, the energy spectrum showing bound states, and plots comparing fluctuation ($\epsilon^2$) and the trade-off relation between $\langle Pangle$, $\langle\etaangle$, and $\epsilon$ across different time scales.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by defining the system and cycle, deriving the necessary statistical tools (characteristic functions, expectation values), comparing exact non-Markovian results to the Born-Markov benchmark, and finally analyzing the optimal conditions near quantum criticality.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical understanding of how non-Markovian quantum dynamics can enhance the performance metrics (efficiency, power) and stability (reduced variance) of fundamental thermodynamic engines, which is crucial for quantum energy technology.
